rationale: OWNER RULING 2026-08-10 (COMMISSION_2026-08-10_owner_rulings_five_pieces.md, item 5): 'yes, let diagnosis loop see the orchestration states file.' The diagnosis loop's evidence bundle renders a '## Schema (live tables)' section so the verdict names real tables/columns instead of guessing. That section is produced by gatherSchema in diagnose_load_runtime_action.go and is passed through a relevance include filter (site%|page%|content%|flow%). Measured against the live DB on 2026-08-10, that include selects 26 of 433 public tables. The defect is that FIVE of the SIX tables this same action renders evidence rows FROM fall outside the include: agent_error_log, orchestration_states, agent_definitions, llm_call_log and code_symbols (only site_work_items matches). So the bundle shows the verdicter rows from six tables while describing the columns of one. The section is also silent about being filtered: it is headed 'Schema (live tables)', stops, and says nothing about a filter, so a table that was filtered out and a table that does not exist render IDENTICALLY. The verdict prompt's cite-or-abstain rule then acts on that absence. This is not theoretical: 090 run 074beb8a-adb4-4074-905a-cb0f857e7f85 (bugs_open/236) returned UNVERIFIABLE with 'the orchestration_states table isn't in the bundle's Schema section, so its real primary-key/id column is unknown and must be confirmed by a human before requerying; guessing again would likely fail the same way'. It had queried WHERE id = ...; the column is orchestration_id. TWO separate 236 runs died this way, and the resulting UNVERIFIABLE reads to a casual eye like 'your premise was wrong' when in fact the loop could not address the table at all. The intent of this change is narrow and is OBSERVABILITY OF THE EVIDENCE CORPUS, not a change to diagnosis logic: (1) the tables this action draws evidence from are always listed, whatever the include says, so the bundle can never show a row from a table whose columns it hides; (2) the section states that it is filtered, how many tables of how many are shown, and how to reach an unlisted table without a human. The commission explicitly warned against a hard-coded table list ('a hard-coded table list is the same drift class this estate keeps filing... adding orchestration_states fixes today and leaves the next missing table to be discovered the same expensive way'), so the always-list is DERIVED and its derivation is enforced by a test that re-scans this action's own SQL and fails when a query names a table the list does not carry. BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED FOR THE REVIEWER TO CHECK: gatherSchema has exactly ONE caller (grep across the repo, non-test); the four live agents carrying a diagnose_load_runtime step (diagnose-agent, diagnose-wiring-probe-pass/ok/bad) set NONE of schema_include_patterns / schema_exclude_patterns / schema_full, so all four run the Go defaults and no live config overrides this; the listing grows from 26 to 31 tables, verified by running the new SQL live; the five added tables cost ~3,175 chars against a current section of 8,819 and a whole bundle of ~80,000, so ~+4% on the bundle; schema_table_cap is 120 and the listing is at 31, so the cap is not approached. CONSUMERS TOLD, NOT MERELY MEASURED (owner ruling 2026-07-29 #3): the only consumer of this string is diagnose_assemble_bundle_action.go, which renders it under '## Schema (live tables)' at :306 for the diagnosis verdict step; what changes for that consumer is that the section now carries a leading '>' notice line before the table listing and lists five more tables. No other pipeline reads runtime.schema. SCOPE ROUTING (owner ruling 2026-08-10 item 4, PROCESS_architecture_review.md as worded 'it adds, changes or removes an exported symbol other packages depend on'): every symbol touched here is UNEXPORTED and package-local (gatherSchema, schemaAlwaysTables, schemaFilterNotice, stringsAsIface), the new config key is one action's step config rather than a shared vocabulary, and nothing changes what a shared mechanism GUARANTEES (owner ruling 2026-07-29 #1). So this is council-gate scope, not architecture review. Verification is deliberately disconfirmable and is NOT 'the table appears in the bundle text': the commission requires re-running a 090 whose evidence lives in orchestration_states and confirming its data_request executes instead of erroring 42703. That run is bugs_open/236 and it is blocked on a fleet roll, because Go changes are inert until an image ships.

plan.summary: The diagnosis bundle's Schema section is built by a relevance include that selects 26 of 433 live tables, and five of the six tables the same action renders evidence rows from fall outside it — so the bundle shows rows from tables whose columns it hides. The section also never says it is filtered, making a filtered-out table indistinguishable from a non-existent one; 090 run 074beb8a consequently guessed a column name on orchestration_states, got SQLSTATE 42703, and stopped at UNVERIFIABLE asking for a human. This change (1) adds an always-list of the tables this action itself queries, which beats both filters and sorts first so the table cap cannot reach it, (2) prints a notice stating the listing is filtered, its coverage, and how to read an unlisted table via the existing read-only data_request channel, and (3) adds a test that re-derives the always-list from this file's own SQL so it cannot go stale the way the include did.

edits.rationale: The list of tables this action renders evidence rows from, which must always appear in the Schema section. Declared once in Go and reused as the InputSpec default via stringsAsIface, because a spec default plus a Go var holding the same list is two hand-maintained copies of one fact — the exact drift class that produced this bug (the include list was correct when written and silently wrong once the gather grew sections reading other tables).

Take an `always` list and OR it AROUND the existing filter conditions rather than AND-ing it in, so neither the relevance include nor the exclude denylist can drop an evidence table; and order always-tables first so tableCap truncation cannot reach them either. Bound as a text[] parameter, never interpolated. An empty slice binds '{}' so `= ANY` matches nothing — the degenerate case is 'no always-tables', never 'every table'.
edits.sketch:
-func gatherSchema(ctx, db, exclude, include []string, full bool, tableCap int)
+func gatherSchema(ctx, db, exclude, include, always []string, full bool, tableCap int)

-	query := "SELECT table_name, column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE " +
-		strings.Join(conds, " AND ") + " ORDER BY table_name, ordinal_position"
+	query := fmt.Sprintf(`SELECT table_name, column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns
+		WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND (%s OR %s)
+		ORDER BY (table_name = ANY($%d::text[])) DESC, table_name, ordinal_position`,
+		filterCond, alwaysCond, alwaysParam)

edits.rationale: Makes the filtering legible so an absence reads as 'filtered', not 'does not exist'. The final sentence is the load-bearing one: it tells the verdicter it can reach an unlisted table through the read-only data_request channel it already has, which is precisely what 074beb8a declined to do when it asked for a human instead. Suppressed when schema_full is set or nothing was withheld, so the notice can never be a false claim about the listing; a failed total-count degrades to silence rather than printing a fabricated denominator.

The anti-staleness control the commission asked for. It re-derives the table set from this action's own SQL and fails when a query names a table the always-list does not carry, so the next evidence section added cannot silently reintroduce the blindness. Two deliberate properties: comments are STRIPPED before scanning (a source-scanning test otherwise makes prose load-bearing — this file's comments name orchestration_states, and a scan reading them would pass by quoting itself), and the scan reads only backtick literals, with a separate guard that FAILS if SELECT...FROM appears in a double-quoted string the scan cannot read — a guard that passes while blind is the failure shape being guarded against. Proven disconfirmable by mutation: removing orchestration_states from the list fails both this test and the determinism test.

The behavioural half, via sqlmock (already used across this package). Asserts against the SQL actually issued that an always-table survives BOTH a denylist pattern that would drop it AND an include that does not match it, that the always-list is BOUND rather than interpolated, and that the ORDER BY puts always-tables first. A unit test of the Go filtering alone would have passed on the broken version too, which is why the assertion is on the statement.

plan.risks: 1. BUNDLE SIZE. The section grows by ~3,175 chars (the five tables' column listings), measured from information_schema, against a current section of 8,819 and a whole bundle of ~80,000 — about +4%. schema_table_cap is 120 and the listing moves 26 -> 31, so the cap is not approached. No total-bundle cap exists; caps in diagnose_assemble_bundle are per-section (max_body_chars 60000 on symbol bodies, siblingSigCap 6000, workflowStepCap 8000) and none of them bound this string. 2. THE ALWAYS-LIST BEATS AN OPERATOR'S EXPLICIT DENYLIST. Deliberate: these are the tables the bundle shows rows from, and hiding their columns is never the right answer. Reviewers should say if they disagree — the alternative (exclude wins) reintroduces exactly this bug the moment someone adds a '%log%' pattern, which would silently drop agent_error_log and llm_call_log. Note also that configStringSlice treats an empty array as 'absent' and returns the default, so the list cannot be disabled by setting it to []; that is fail-safe but it does mean the only way to shrink it is to name a different non-empty list. 3. THE NOTICE IS PROMPT-ADJACENT TEXT read by an LLM verdicter. It tells the model it may issue a data_request against information_schema.columns. That channel already exists and is already read-only-enforced at three layers (verdict prompt instruction, IsReadOnlySQL lint at both the route and gather layers, and a BeginTx ReadOnly transaction which is the real guarantee), so this widens what the model KNOWS it can do, not what it CAN do. A reviewer should still check that the wording cannot be read as licence to query outside that channel. 4. THE COUNT QUERY is one extra information_schema round trip per gather; it is unindexed catalogue access but bounded and runs once per diagnosis iteration, alongside the far larger columns query already there. On failure it degrades to no notice rather than a wrong denominator. 5. VERIFICATION IS NOT YET DONE and is not claimed: the change is inert until a chassis image ships, and the real test — re-running a 090 whose evidence lives in orchestration_states and confirming its data_request executes instead of erroring 42703 — needs a fleet roll. Checking that the table appears in the bundle text is explicitly NOT sufficient per the commission.
